title: Knee replacement
what: The surgeon replaces the worn surfaces of the joint with artificial ones, called a prosthesis. The surgery is done under general anesthesia or a spinal anesthetic.
why: When the joint is badly damaged, usually by arthritis, the pain makes walking hard, and treatment without surgery does not help.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the hospital stay is usually 3 to 7 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
Any infection: teeth, skin, or urinary tract. These are treated before surgery
If you ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, knee X-rays, a check by a general doctor, and sometimes a dentist. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: An anesthesiologist will talk with you, and together you will choose the type of pain relief.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Before surgery, remove rugs and cords from the floor, and put things you need at an easy height. Get crutches or a walker.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Stop smoking at least a few weeks before. Wounds heal better this way.

bring: Your ID, referral, and test results
Comfortable clothes and closed shoes with no back, with Velcro straps
Crutches or a walker, if your clinic asks
steps: On the day of surgery, you change into a gown and an IV is put into a vein
The anesthesiologist puts you to sleep or gives an injection in your back. Your legs go numb
The surgeon makes a cut over the knee
The damaged parts of the bone are removed and the prosthesis is put in
The wound is stitched and a dressing is put on
You are taken to the recovery room, and then to your ward
feel: After surgery the knee hurts and swells. You will get pain relief
After a spinal anesthetic, your legs may stay numb for a few hours
The first steps are hard. This is normal
after: Staff usually help you stand up with a walker the very next day
Do your knee exercises every day. This matters most for a good result
You will get medicine against blood clots, as the doctor prescribes
Crutches or a cane are usually needed for a few weeks
Most people walk with confidence after 6 to 12 weeks
Stitches are removed after about 2 weeks, unless they dissolve
red_flags: Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services
Your calf is swollen and painful
A temperature above 38 degrees, redness, pus, or fluid from the wound
Knee pain that suddenly gets much worse

faq.q: How long does a knee replacement last?
faq.a: Usually 15 to 20 years or longer. A lot depends on your weight and activity.

faq.q: When can I walk after a knee replacement?
faq.a: With a walker, usually the next day. Without support, after a few weeks, when the doctor allows.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your ID, test results, medicine list, and things. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
